A.summary: Comenius, writing from Leszno during the Swedish invasion of Poland, ends his report to Rákóczi's councillor Klobusiczky with one ciphered sentence: 'Nothing is more certain than that Poland has perished, and the papacy in it.' The letter around it reports the Swedish advance from Poznań on Warsaw and the flight of the Catholic clergy. Comenius was then pressing George II Rákóczi of Transylvania to side with Sweden (background, not taken from this letter).
A.en:
Nothing is more certain than that Poland has perished, and the papacy in it.

The good man [iyy?] is wonderfully troubled by the great delays put in his way.

B.summary: The cipher stands in a letter in which Comenius quotes news from a friend in England (23 Apr 1655): Schaum has not yet arrived there, the Polish and Swedish envoys in London, the Waldensian massacre in Piedmont, the fleet in America. The cipher follows this news and comes before a postscript ('Tandem apulit [...] dominus Schaum') that seems to belong to the same English letter; the letter then goes on and closes 'Raptissime 24 Maji 1655'. The cipher itself is not deciphered.

system: Document A: reciprocal letter substitution, the Rákóczi envoys' table printed in MHH XXIII p. 740 (a=m, b=i, c=p ...), word division kept, 'et' in clear; the printed text also has the digits 6, 9, 5 for i, n, l (probably misread b, q, h); document B: system…
